title: Which statements does the height table justify?
description: Six statements about the average heights of boys and girls in India are tested against a table for four years. The video finds the cells each statement needs and says which statements the table justifies. Keeko thinks a higher average means every girl is taller.
teaching_notes: One idea: to test a statement, find the cells it talks about and compare only those. Watch for students who treat an average as if it described every child.

source: Test the six statements against the table of average heights
video_script.why: The child can read a table of averages and now tests statements against it.
video_script.substitution: The book's own table of average heights of boys and girls in India for 1989, 1999, 2009 and 2019.
video_script.anchor: Table of average heights in cm, ages 5 to 19, four years. Cells used: age 19 boys 163.5 (1989), 166.5 (2019); 15-year-old boys 2019: 159; 16-year-old boys 1989: 158.9; 13-year-old girls 1989: 143.2; 14-year-old girls 2009: 148; age 11 in 2019: boys 137, girls 138.6; boys aged 18 and 19 in 2019: 166, 166.5.
video_script.wrong_answer: all girls aged thirteen are taller than all girls aged eleven
video_script.wrong_move: Treats a higher average as if every girl in the older group is taller than every girl in the younger group.
video_script.payoff_line: Only statements one and three are justified by the table.

final_answer.value: Justified: 1 and 3; not justified: 2, 4 and 5; 6 cannot be decided from the table
final_answer.spoken: only statements one and three are justified; two, four and five are not; six cannot be decided from the table

maths_rules: statement 1 justified: both columns higher in 2019 than in 1989 at every age, for example age 19 boys 163.5 to 166.5 and girls 151.9 to 155.2 (some ages dipped slightly in between)
statement 2 not justified: 13-year-old girls in 1989 are 143.2, less than 14-year-old girls in 2009 at 148
statement 3 justified: 15-year-old boys in 2019 are 159, more than 16-year-old boys in 1989 at 158.9
statement 4 not justified: averages say nothing about every girl
statement 5 not justified: girls' averages are higher at ages 11 and 12 in every year, for example 2019 age 11, 138.6 against 137
statement 6 not decidable: the table stops at 19; in 2019 boys grew only 166.5 - 166 = 0.5 cm from 18 to 19
video_script.design: One idea: find the cells a statement compares, and compare only those. The table sits in the anchor; on the board each statement points to its own cells and ends justified, not justified, or not decidable.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about the heights of children in India.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A table gives average heights of boys and girls from age five to nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Six statements are made about the table.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which of them can the table justify?

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>To test a statement, find the cells it talks about.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Then compare only those cells.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>If the cells are not in the table, the table cannot decide.

beats.on_screen: Given: average heights (cm) for ages 5 to 19 in 1989, 1999, 2009, 2019; six statements

marks.m1: the table is summarised in one line and the six statements are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, a table of averages for four years, and six statements.

beats.on_screen: To find: which statements the table justifies
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to test each of the six statements against the table.

beats.on_screen: Statement 1: age 19 boys 163.5 (1989) to 166.5 (2019); every age is higher in 2019. Statement 3: 15-year-old boys 2019: 159 > 16-year-old boys 1989: 158.9

marks.m1: statement one is written with its two years
marks.m3: a tick is placed on every age row for 2019
marks.m4: statement three is written with its two cells

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, test statements one and three. Statement one says every average rose from nineteen eighty nine to twenty nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>At age nineteen, boys were one hundred and sixty three point five. In twenty nineteen they were one hundred and sixty six point five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Every age is higher in the last year.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Statement three compares two cells.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Boys aged fifteen in twenty nineteen average one hundred and fifty nine. Boys aged sixteen in nineteen eighty nine average one hundred and fifty eight point nine.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>One hundred and fifty nine is more, and both statements are justified.

marks.m4: 143.2 < 148 is written and statement two is crossed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, test statement two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Girls aged thirteen in nineteen eighty nine average one hundred and forty three point two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Girls aged fourteen in two thousand nine average one hundred and forty eight.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>One hundred and forty three point two is less, so statement two is not justified.

beats.on_screen: Statement 4 is about every girl, not about an average. Statement 5: age 11 in 2019, girls 138.6, boys 137

marks.m2: the words about every girl, not about an average appear
marks.m4: age 11 in 2019 is circled with girls 138.6 and boys 137
marks.m5: girls lead is written and statement five is crossed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, test statements four and five. Statement four is about every single girl.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The table gives averages, not each girl. Statement four is not justified.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Statement five says boys average more at every age.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Look at age eleven in twenty nineteen. Girls average one hundred and thirty eight point six, and boys one hundred and thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The girls lead, so statement five is not justified.

beats.on_screen: Statement 6: the table stops at age 19; in 2019 boys 166 at 18 and 166.5 at 19, only 0.5 cm more

marks.m2: the table's last row at age 19 is marked
marks.m3: 166 and 166.5 are written with the gap 0.5
marks.m4: the words not in the table appear beyond the last row

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, test statement six. It talks about boys beyond age nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The table stops at age nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In twenty nineteen, boys grew only half a centimetre from eighteen to nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The table has no cells beyond nineteen, so we cannot decide.

beats.on_screen: Answer: justified: 1 and 3; not justified: 2, 4 and 5; 6 cannot be decided from the table

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Only statements one and three are justified by the table.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Statements two, four and five are not justified.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Statement six cannot be decided from the table.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks all girls aged thirteen are taller than all girls aged eleven, since their average is higher.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>An average describes the group, not every girl in it.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Some eleven year olds can be taller than some thirteen year olds.
